articles.title: Wisconsin women beat Grambling, winning margin largest in 20 years | Takeaways
articles.summary: The Badgers women's basketball team improved to 3-0 with a victory over Grambling that included some notable statistical benchmarks.
articles.body:
MADISON – Wisconsin closed out a busy first week of the season with a 97-46 victory over Grambling State on Nov. 8 at the Kohl Center. It was the program's largest margin of victory in almost 20 years.

The victory, which improved the Badgers women's basketball team's record to 3-0, equaled the margin of victory set by an 88-37 win over Southern Mississippi on Dec. 1, 2006.

But that wasn't the only noteworthy mark from the victory.

The Badgers also held the Tigers (0-3) to 25% shooting (14 for 56). That ties for the 10th-lowest all-time lowest field goal percentage for a UW opponent.

UW's 33 first-quarter points set a mark for the highest first quarter in program history while also tying for the second-highest point total in any quarter.

Wisconsin 's 58 points in the first half tied for the seventh most all-time.

Despite the lopsided aspects of the game, the day offered plenty of teaching points for coach Robin Pingeton whose team completed a six-day run that included three games.

Wisconsin had good stretches of ball movement and passing, but in the fourth quarter, the Badgers were outscored, 12-11, and held to 3-for-13 shooting.

"The expectations are higher than that," Pingeton said. "I felt like we gave up too many second-shot opportunities. I thought we handled their pressure well but then had some careless turnovers. The consistency that we've got to play with has got to improve."

Junior guard Teagan Mallegni led the Badgers in scoring for third time, finishing with 22 points on 9-for-13 shooting that included 2 for 4 from 3-point range.

The team's second and third-leading scorers were junior guard Addie Deal (14 points, three assists) and freshman guard Adaline Sheplee (13 points, five rebounds).

This, however, was a day for the team's lesser-used players or players returning from injury/illness to get minutes. Senior Laci Steele (24:19), sophomore Nikki Kerstein (21:06) and freshmen Leah Nordin (16:37) and freshman Giselle Janowski (18:44) posted season highs for minutes.

Wisconsin women's basketball beat Bradley in season opener at Kohl Center

UW's best quarter was the first quarter when it shot 61.9% (13 for 21) and Deal and Mallegni combined for 16 points on 6-for-10 shooting that included 3 for 4 from 3-point range.

What was notable about the Badgers' play was their passing. Eleven of their baskets came off assists. Seven players had an assist in the quarter.

"I thought there were possessions we made too many extra passes and just didn't take advantage of shots that we needed to take," Pingeton said. "But that's good, right? As a coach, you appreciate the unselfish play."

Badgers' board work, shooting must improve

In a game filled with so many notable statistical marks, there were a couple of oddities:

Despite winning by 51 points, the Badgers held just a one board edge in rebounding, 42-41.

Wisconsin almost scored 100 points but didn't crack 50% shooting. The Badgers shot 49.3% against Grambling.

Improvement in those areas is part of Pingeton's wish list for her team after one week of the season.

"We haven't shot the ball well to be honest with you. We can shoot better. Must get sharper," she said. "Defensively (we have) good stretches but we can be better. Rebounding we can be better. I want to see growth, but I'm excited about heart posture of locker room."

articles.title: Connor Hellebuyck's Status for Devils vs. Jets Revealed, Goalie's 1st Trip to Winnipeg Since Trade
articles.summary: Connor Hellebuyck will have to wait to go up against his former team for the first time since being traded.
articles.body:
Connor Hellebuyck will have to wait to go up against his former team for the first time since being traded.

The New Jersey Devils announced Sunday that the goalie won't play against the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday despite being "adamant" about playing in his former city.

Terrible Contracts Teams Wish They Could Dump 🤦‍♂️

Hellebuyck spent the first 11 seasons of his career in Winnipeg, but made it clear he was unhappy with how things were going during his exit interview in April.

"From my perspective, complacency is not going to get us moving forward," he told reporters . "So something has got to happen. I'm not going to just sit here and throw every guy under the bus because, honestly, I'm a goalie and I know goaltending really well.

"I can't say, 'Well, this forward did this and that defenceman did that.' That's not my spot. I believe in every guy giving their A-plus effort every single night. As a teammate, I can really rally behind that and really cherish those moments with those guys. But to just put that same product on the ice, I don't think it worked for a reason."

In August, he confirmed that he had requested a trade from the Jets, setting up what would be a messy exit. Hellebuyck was suspended by the team in September after informing the Jets that he would not attend training camp.

The saga ended on Oct. 24 when Winnipeg traded him to Detroit in return for goaltender Nico Daws, forward Dawson Mercer, center Alexander Command, center Nick Bjugstad and two future draft picks.

It surely would have been an emotional return for Hellebuyck, considering all the time he spent with the Jets and the way things ended, but he won't be on the ice in his first game against his former team.

Still, it will be interesting to get more perspective on the situation when he addresses the media.

articles.title: China construye su primer prototipo de un avión eléctrico: tiene 19 plazas, con alcance de 500 km y una velocidad de 402 km/h
articles.standfirst: Comac es la empresa responsable de este avance tecnológico
articles.summary: Comac es la empresa responsable de este avance tecnológico
articles.body: El campo de la energía en los aviones es aún un libro con las páginas en blanco. El pasado lunes, 2 de noviembre, el medio especializado Aviation International News (AIN) informó de que Coma estaba finalizando su prototipo a escala real de un avión eléctrico. Y es que la empresa ya se habría especializado totalmente en este tipo de aeronaves. El pasado así lo atestigua: han conseguido confeccionar el avión regional ARJ21, el avión de medio alcance C919, y con el avión de largo alcance C929. Ahora bien, esta tarea es aún más complicada. Este avión recibe el nombre de CE-25A. La primera imagen filtrada ya habría confirmado la primera característica con los otros aviones: su forma de T en la cola. Desde AIN, dejan entrever que esta forma tiene algo escondido mucho más allá que un simple cambio de imagen: “Este diseño sugiere que Comac podría estar utilizando un sistema de propulsión eléctrica distribuida”. Aunque esto es un rumor, lo que sí está prácticamente confirmado es que tiene 19 plazas, con alcance de 500 km y una velocidad de 402 km/h. Hay que tener en cuenta que para entender este proceso, hay que echar un vistazo al pasado. El proyecto de desarrollo CE-25A se presentó en 2023 en Shanghái. Y lo hizo como una aeronave de pequeño tamaño, pensada para transportar pasajeros en distancias relativamente cortas. De ahí que solo cuente con capacidad para 19 viajeros. Basándonos en las infraestructuras de la actualidad, sería un avión pensado para conectar ciudades próximas, aeropuertos regionales o localidades que no necesitan aviones comerciales grandes. Es decir, rutas de unos 200-400 km, aunque eso dependería de las reservas de energía. Si lo extrapolamos a España, serviría para conectar Madrid con cualquier otro punto del país.

articles.title: Lando Norris wins Sao Palo Grand Prix, but Mercedes seal constructors title
articles.summary: Norris wins from pole position on a rainy Sao Paulo track as Mercedes win team title for the first time since 2021.
articles.body:
Mercedes have secured ⁠⁠their ninth Formula One constructors world championship ⁠⁠and completed a title double in a wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix won by McLaren’s Lando Norris from pole position for the second year in a row.

The title, secured on Sunday, was the first team crown for Mercedes since 2021 and came a week after 20-year-old Italian Kimi Antonelli made headlines ⁠⁠as the youngest drivers champion with four races to spare.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen finished second, putting on a masterclass from 21st on the grid due to engine penalties in a race that started and ended in the rain.

Teammate Isack Hadjar was third with George Russell fourth for Mercedes and Antonelli fifth with the fastest lap. After leading at the start, both made costly errors on an eventful afternoon.

Mercedes had needed to score only three points more than Ferrari to clinch the title, and the Italian team never threatened to prolong the fight on a treacherous track with Charles Leclerc eighth after a post-race penalty demoted him one place and Lewis Hamilton ninth in his 400th race.

“It was a very tough race, very, very tough,” Norris, the 2025 world champion, said of his 14th career win and 50th podium as well as his team’s first victory since August when ‌‌he won the Dutch Grand Prix.

“A lot of challenges today with the conditions and going onto slicks in the wet is always tough, especially when you are pushing for the lead and trying to catch up a little bit,” added the Briton, who lost out to Antonelli when the start lights went out.

“The main thing today was I kept it cool and didn’t make any mistakes and had the pace when I needed to. Nice to be back on the top step and what a place to do it as well.”

Norris took the chequered flag, waved by Brazilian football forward Neymar, 14.602 seconds clear of Driver of the Day Verstappen.

Mercedes, whose engines also power McLaren, have now equalled Williams’ nine constructors championships.

“It was a very strong beginning of the season, and that kind of got us ⁠⁠over the line,” team boss Toto Wolff said. “These last few races have been challenging at times. Today it was difficult, but overall, ⁠⁠I’m so proud of the organisation.”

McLaren’s Oscar Piastri was sixth with Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson seventh after a fine race that saw the New Zealander start third and run in second place for the first five laps.

Nico Hulkenberg took the final point for Audi in a race of spins, slippery moments and changeable conditions.

Verstappen moved further ahead in the driver standings in the race for second place overall, now 17 points clear of Russell, who ⁠⁠moved up to third.

articles.title: Rejected a job offer for chess, now India's 100th Grandmaster: How Anuj Shrivatri became Madhya Pradesh's first GM
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: While India was preparing to light diyas for Diwali, Anuj Shrivatri was about 2,800 miles away, in a tournament hall in the Philippines,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: While India was preparing to light diyas for Diwali, Anuj Shrivatri was about 2,800 miles away, in a tournament hall in the Philippines, closing out a game that would make him the country's 100th Grandmaster and the first his state, Madhya Pradesh, had ever produced.Before this Sunday, India had 99 Grandmasters, and Madhya Pradesh had none. The tally has now gone up by one, thanks to a 22-year-old from Katni who rejected a corporate job offer to chase this exact moment.As he prepares to board a flight back home, his latest challenge is to contain the euphoria felt in his voice."The feeling right now is mostly relief," Anuj told TimesofIndia.com from the Philippines, barely a day after winning the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship and securing the GM title."I had been trying for the GM title for a long time. There were so many times my GM norms were missed. At least four or five times I was really close, and it slipped away. So now that the title is finally complete, I'm feeling a lot of relief."Shrivatri's parents, Ashok Kumar Shrivatri, a teacher with the railways, and Manorama Shrivatri, a teacher at a government school, had lived through every one of those near misses alongside him, making this ve occasion all the more special."They're very happy. They also know I'd been struggling with this for a long time. I was playing well, but sometimes the results just weren't coming. Now that the title is finally complete, they're very happy. And since it happened during Diwali, it's an even bigger joy for them," he added with a smile.A father's hobby, a son's careerChess entered Shrivatri's life through a parent's old college pastime."My father used to play chess during his college days," he recalled. "He was quite fond of the game, so when I was young, around five or six, he introduced me to it. Then both my elder brother and I took a liking to it."His brother eventually drifted away from the board; he now works as a software engineer in Bengaluru. Shrivatri didn't.A succession of coaches shaped him from there. Virendra Tiwari, who taught him his very first moves, then Nikhilesh Jain, then Yashpal Arora, and finally Rajesh Bahadur, under whose guidance Shrivatri became an International Master (IM) in 2019.After that, he says, it was mostly self-directed work, punctuated by sessions with respected Grandmasters such as Vishnu Prasanna, Swayams Mishra and Swapnil Dhopade whenever he needed outside eyes on his game.What followed the IM title, though, wasn't a straight climb."After 2019, I was very motivated, but then Covid came," he continued. "After that, I wasn't sure whether to pursue chess as a career or focus on my studies. At that point, chess didn't feel certain enough, and I wasn't sure of myself either, so I decided to focus on studies."He completed his BTech degree in Computer Science at Lovely Professional University, and it was only in 2025, playing tournaments on the side, almost as an afterthought, that something shifted."I felt a change in my play, in my temperament. I thought, no, I should give chess a real shot, give it a year or two and try to become a GM," he recalled.The timing forced a genuine choice. His college internship ended just as a full-time job offer from the company landed in his inbox."I was fairly certain by then that completing the GM title would be a great thing," he revealed. "So I quit the company and went full-time into chess."The price of chasing the dreamThe decision to go full-time in chess came with its challenges. With no sponsorship, every trip abroad came out of his own pocket, financed in large part by what he earned playing rapid tournaments and coaching gigs."Finances were the biggest struggle, because I was managing everything myself and there was no sponsorship as such. I was earning money from rapid tournaments and spending it on trips abroad," he admitted.That math also explains why getting an opportunity to play against elite, 2600-plus-rated opposition has been difficult."The strong players are usually found in very niche tournaments, a big event in Kazakhstan, or a strong open in Qatar. But going there is financially a very risky decision. One tournament can cost around a lakh rupees just to go and play," he added.Becoming a Grandmaster despite losing in Round 1In the Philippines, Shrivatri lost his opening-round game. He feels what went wrong was his decision to play aggressively as Black."I took on too much risk, and my position became very uncomfortable. I think it was simply the fault of my opening," he recalled.He rebuilt from there with a complete change of approach."For the rest of the games, I played very solid with Black. I told myself I'd try to create chances, but if it didn't work out and my opponent played well, it was fine to take the draw. That approach helped me a lot, because at some point or another, people make mistakes. You just have to wait for them."What followed was an unbeaten run in his remaining eight games, with six wins and two draws. He finished the tournament with 7/9, half a point ahead of second-placed Vietnamese GM Nguyen Duc Hoa.'Satisfied isn't really the right word'Hailing from the same city, Akshat Khamparia, the state’s first IM, recalls a boy who was reserved away from the board but unusually mature on it.Even as a youngster, he leaned on patience and structure rather than fireworks, picking apart positions move by careful move long before he had the rating to back that style up.Khamparia, MP Chess's committee convener who has spent years building up its tournament circuit, has made a habit of promoting the state's young players at every event he runs, with banners with their faces up at venues."We've done a lot for Anuj too," Khamparia said. "We've highlighted him everywhere, in events, at every opportunity we get."It's the same persistence that, separately, saw Khamparia spend years nudging Shrivatri toward the career security of a sports-quota job with Indian Railways.And after years of him pushing Anuj, the process has now gone through. Anuj’s medical has been completed, and his joining Western Railway is in its final stages.Even now, Shrivatri resists calling himself satisfied."Satisfied isn't really the right word," he said, "because I have a pretty strong opinion that you should never become complacent in life. You should enjoy the milestone, of course, but in general, you should never settle. That's something I try to follow."So, what is next for him? The 22-year-old concluded, "There are two things I'm sure about. I want to cross a 2600 rating, and I want to win as many tournaments as I can. Those are my two goals in chess right now."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sports Personality of the Year 2026: Date announced - and audience to have more influence than ever
articles.summary: BBC Sports Personality of the Year will be held on 13 December - and audiences will have more influence than ever over the awards.
articles.body:
The 2026 BBC Sports Personality of the Year show will be held on Sunday, 13 December - with five winners decided by public votes.

Clare Balding, Gabby Logan and Alex Scott will again host the programme, which will be hosted in Salford and broadcast live on BBC One, BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app from 17:45 GMT.

Five of the nine awards to be presented on the night will be decided by public vote.

The show will celebrate another great year of sport, including Team GB's most successful Winter Olympics, England's best finish at a men's Fifa World Cup since 1966, and record-breaking displays at the European Athletics Championships.

There will be two new award categories at the ceremony this year - Men's Footballer of the Year and BBC World Service Women's Footballer of the Year.

The latter has been a BBC World Service award since 2015 but will now be presented as part of the BBC Sports Personality of the Year awards for the first time. Voting - for global audiences - opens on Tuesday, 10 November.

In addition to crowning the winners of both football awards, fans will also select the winners of the World Sport Star of the Year, Team of the Year and Sports Personality of the Year award itself.

An independent panel made up of industry experts, sports broadcasters, sports journalists and former sportspeople will determine the shortlists for the Sports Personality of the Year, Team of the Year and World Sports Star awards, with the winners chosen by public votes. The independent panel will also determine the winners of Young Sports Personality of the Year and Coach of the Year.

Separate panels of football experts will provide the shortlist of contenders for Men's Footballer of the Year and Women's Footballer of the Year.

Alex Kay-Jelski - director of BBC Sport - said: "What I love about BBC Sports Personality of the Year is that it brings together all those moments that stopped us in our tracks. The goals, the medals, the upsets, the records, the stories that had us talking at work, in the pub and around the dinner table.

"And what a year we've had. This year's shortlists will be packed with athletes and teams who have achieved extraordinary things, but what's especially exciting is that audiences will have a bigger say than ever before in who takes home the trophies."

Full voting details, dates and T&Cs will be announced in due course.

articles.standfirst: Hoy nos parece lo más natural del mundo, pero la disposición de los tres pedales del coche no siempre fue así. Un modelo de 1916 tuvo mucho que ver en que acabáramos conduciendo de esta manera
articles.summary: Hoy nos parece lo más natural del mundo, pero la disposición de los tres pedales del coche no siempre fue así. Un modelo de 1916 tuvo mucho que ver en que acabáramos conduciendo de esta manera
articles.body: Hay cosas que hacemos tantas veces y de una manera tan interiorizada, que las hacemos sin pensar. Como subirnos al coche, ponernos el cinturón (en esto, algunos fallan), girar la llave o pulsar el botón de arranque e ir accionando tres pedales que ni sabemos por qué están así: el embrague a la izquierda, el freno en el centro y el acelerador a la derecha. Pero hubo una época en la que los coches eran casi un laboratorio de inventos y cada fabricante montaba a su manera elementos que hoy nos parecen intocables. Y en este sentido, la disposición de los mandos no era un asunto cerrado... hasta que en 1916 llegó el Cadillac Type 53 y presentó una solución que empezó a gustar a conductores y resto de fabricantes. Eso, y no su diseño, su rendimiento o su lujo, es por lo que hoy día se recuerda a este modelo americano. Hasta entonces, los fabricantes habían probado con diferentes combinaciones de palancas y pedales, de forma que conducir un coche podía convertirse en una pequeña aventura si uno estaba acostumbrado a otro distinto. El famosísimo Ford T, por ejemplo, ya tenía pedal de freno, pero el acelerador se accionaba mediante una palanca situada junto al propio volante. Pero este Cadillac Type 53 presentó una configuración de tres pedles con embrague, freno y acelerador, de izquierda a derecha. Además, tenía la palanca de cambios y el freno de mano entre los asientos delanteros, y en lugar de tener que girar una palanca en el morro del coche para ponerlo en marcha, bastaba girar una llave desde dentro del habitáculo. Pero ¿por qué ese orden y no otro? Lo curioso es que, en una época en la que la seguridad al volante parecía no importarle a nadie, la respuesta tiene bastante sentido desde el punto de vista de la seguridad. El embrague necesita un pie para él solo porque puede necesitar combinarse con una pisada al freno, y su función es interrumpir la conexión entre el motor y la transmisión para poder cambiar de marcha o detener el vehículo sin que se cale. En los coches manuales, por tanto, tiene mucho sentido que tenga un pie solo a su disposición. El pie derecho se encarga del acelerador y del freno. Son dos acciones que por lo general (salvo que seas piloto y ruedes en circuito) no necesitamos realizar al mismo tiempo, sino de forma alternativa. Si quieres ganar velocidad, pisas el acelerador; cuando necesitas reducirla, trasladas el pie al freno. Además, colocar el acelerador a la derecha permite mantener el pie en una posición natural cuando no estamos frenando, mientras que el freno queda suficientemente cerca para pasar de un pedal a otro con rapidez. La solución resultó tan natural, que poco a poco se fue volviendo universal. Desde aquel Cadillac de 1916 los coches han evolucionado por completo. Tanto, que a nadie le extraña ya leer noticias sobre coches autónomos, lo que deja entrever un futuro a largo plazo de coches sin volantes ni pedales. Pero en 2026 los tres pedales siguen resistiendo, aunque solo en los cada vez menos habituales coches con cambio manual.

articles.title: Josh Turek, el primer senador de EE.UU. con espina bífida, jugó en España y fue medallista paralímpico
articles.standfirst: Militó en Fundosa ONCE, Getafe y Bidaideak Bilbao BSR. Txema Alonso, el presidente del equipo vasco que le fichó, recuerda su figura en MARCA. Bicampeón en Juegos con EE.UU.
articles.summary: Militó en las filas del Fundosa ONCE, Getafe y Bidaideak Bilbao BSR. Con Estados Unidos ganó el oro en los Juegos de Río y Tokio
articles.body: El escaño del Senado de Estados Unidos por Iowa ha estado en manos republicanas desde 2015. Ha sido el bicampeón paralímpico Joshua Turek, que militó durante más de una década en la liga española de baloncesto en silla, quien ha ganado la batalla electoral a Ashley Hinson en uno de los mayores feudos conservadores del país. “Como he dicho siempre, mi historia es verdaderamente el sueño americano”, dijo Turek en su discurso de victoria . “Sólo en Estados Unidos alguien nacido en una familia de clase trabajadora en Council Bluffs, Iowa, que pasó por las dificultades económicas y sanitarias que yo viví, podría finalmente representar a mi país en cuatro Juegos Paralímpicos, ganar dos medallas de oro, representar a mi comunidad en la legislatura de Iowa y, a partir de esta noche, ser elegido para representar al estado en el que nací y crecí en el Senado de los Estados Unidos”, añadió. Turek llegó a España en 2004 para jugar en el entonces Fundosa ONCE -hoy CD ILUNION- donde permaneció siete temporadas y donde recuerdan su versatilidad. Después militó en el Getafe, en el Hyeres francés y, de 2015 hasta la 2019 fue uno de los jugadores más destacados del Bideaideak Bilbao BSR. Con el equipo vasco ganó la Euroliga 1 su último año. En 2017 fue elegido mejor jugador extranjero de la División de Honor, la denominación entonces de la liga española de baloncesto en silla. Siempre dijo que la competición de nuestro país "era la mejor del mundo". Txema Alonso, presidente del Bidaideak Bilbao BSR durante ocho años, fue quien le fichó a petición de Asier García, el capitán. El mandatario atiende amablemente a MARCA para recordar las cuatro temporadas que contaron con el ahora senador: "Era un jugador absolutamente contrastado que había dejado huella en las ligas de Italia, Francia y, por supuesto, en la española. En todas había resaltado por su capacidad anotadora. Llegamos rápido a un acuerdo, creo que porque vio que en Bilbao tenía un reto de los que a él le gustaban, que no era otro que poner fin a su carrera deportiva ayudando a un equipo modesto a situarse en la elite del baloncesto estatal e internacional". Alonso recuerda que destaca el primer minuto en el vestuario de Txurdinaga demostró su entrega y desde el primer partido, que "toda su calidad no residía sólo en su capacidad de anotación, siempre por encima de los 20 puntos, sino también en el control de los tiempos de juego y en los análisis inteligentes de las necesidades tácticas que se precisaban para superar al rival. Esa inteligencia que mostraba en cancha la traslucía también fuera. Persona culta, bien formada y con una capacidad trabajada para hacer análisis profundos, tuve ocasión de charlar muchas veces sobre la situación social y política en el País Vasco y a nivel internacional, y siempre me demostró que era tremendamente equilibrado en sus juicios y pronunciamientos", asegura. En la temporada 17-18, tras perder ante Galatasaray la final de la Euroliga 1, le pidió disculpas por no haber podido llevar la Copa a Bilbao. "Tal era su honradez y humildad", rememora Alonso. "Y me vaticinó que en la siguiente temporada el trofeo sería nuestro. Y así fue, en la primavera de 2019 de Sheffield volvió con ese título". Días después anunció su retirada de la competición de clubes, su vuelta a Estados Unidos y su deseo de terminar su carrera en los Juegos de Tokio con su selección. En una recepción con el Alcalde de Bilbao, en conversación privada, les comentó que tras los Juegos quería dedicarse a la representación política con la ambición de llegar a ser algún día senador de su estado en Washington. Dicho y hecho. "A un modesto equipo bilbaíno le hizo campeón de una competición continental, a Iowa le concede ahora ser, estoy convencido, el mejor de sus representantes", vaticina Alonso. En nuestro país también encontró el amor. Su mujer Jarolin es española y tienen cuatro hijos: Ulette Bonner, Rachell, John y Elisha. Con la selección estadounidense de baloncesto en silla hizo su debut paralímpico en 2004 a los 25 años. Entonces, el equipo perdió en los cuartos de final. Después fue excluido del combinado nacional y regresó para jugar los de Londres 2012 (bronce), Río 2016 (oro) -ganó a España en la final- y Tokio 2020 (oro). Tras la cita japonesa, se retiró y dio el salto a la política. Se postuló para representar a su ciudad natal, Council Bluffs, en la legislatura. En una contienda que Donald Trump ya había ganado dos veces, Josh se esforzó al máximo, subiendo cuestas y escaleras a gatas, para hablar con los habitantes de Iowa de todas las tendencias políticas, y finalmente ganó por seis votos. Fue reelegido y se ha forjado una reputación como legislador sensato y bipartidista. El 3 de noviembre fue elegido primer senador estatal de Estados Unidos con espina bífida. Nació hace 47 años en Council Bluffs (Iowa) con esta condición congénita que afecta el desarrollo de la columna vertebral y la médula espinal. En la biografía de su página web Turek4Iowa achaca esta malformación a que su padre estuviera expuesto al Agente Naranja, una mezcla de herbicidas hormonales altamente tóxicos, durante la Guerra de Vietnam. Josh superó 21 cirugías antes de los 12 años. La silla de ruedas le acompaña desde los 10. De su padre heredó la pasión por el baloncesto, aunque el progenitor no se dedicó a él. "Era pobre y tuvo que trabajar desde los 12 años, por eso nunca tuvo tiempo de practicar lo suficiente para llegar a jugar como profesional, pero tenía talento", explicaba hace unos años el alero del Bidaideak Bilbao BSR a MARCA. Además de Josh, también se han dedicado de forma profesional a este deporte, pero en la modalidad convencional a pie, su hermano John, que ha jugado en media Europa (Holanda, Alemania, Polonia...) y su hermana Elisha, que jugó en la liga española (Canarias, Ibiza, Santiago de Composterla y en Pontevedra). En total, tres de los cinco hermanos. El exjugador de baloncesto contó en campaña con el respaldo del ex presidente Barak Obama, como vimos en un vídeo grabado en una cancha junto a él. "Iowa, has oído al presidente Obama. La pelota está en tu campo. ¡Únete a nuestra campaña y ayúdanos a empujar por el cambio!", decía. Y ahora, como senador, luchará por llevarlo a cabo.
